question: A rope hugs the equator. Add 1 m to its length and raise it evenly all round. Can a cat crawl under?
options: Yes, the gap is about 16 cm
Barely, the gap is about 1 mm
answer: Yes, easily. A circle's circumference is 2π times its radius, so adding 1 m to the rope lifts it by 1 ÷ 2π, about 16 cm, all the way round — whatever the size of the circle. The same extra metre around a football would lift it by the same 16 cm.
move: When the intuition comes from size, check whether size appears in the formula.
trap: One metre spread over 40,000 km feels like nothing at all.
source: Circumference and radius of a circle
reference: Courant & Robbins, What Is Mathematics?, revised by Stewart, Oxford University Press, 1996
